metadata.source: RBI Monetary Policy Department & Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee
metadata.exam_weightage: Extremely High (10-15 Questions across Mains shifts)

standing_deposit_facility_sdf.introduced: April 2022 (replaced fixed reverse repo as floor of LAF corridor)

fixed_reverse_repo_rate.note: Remains in toolkit but SDF is the operative absorption rate

cash_reserve_ratio_crr.basis: Percentage of Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)

statutory_liquidity_ratio_slr.basis: Percentage of Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)

mpc_framework.statutory_basis: Section 45ZB of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (amended by Finance Act, 2016)

rbi_members: Deputy Governor in charge of Monetary Policy (Member)
One Officer of the RBI nominated by the Central Board (Member)
govt_appointed_members: Three external experts appointed by the Central Government on recommendations of Search-cum-Selection Committee (hold office for 4 years, not eligible for re-appointment)

mpc_framework.quorum: 4 members, at least one of whom must be the Governor or in his absence, the Deputy Governor who is the member of the MPC
mpc_framework.voting: Each member has one vote. In case of a tie, the Governor has a second or casting vote.
mpc_framework.meeting_frequency: At least 4 times a year (usually meets bi-monthly: 6 times a year)
mpc_framework.minutes_publication: Minutes of proceedings published on the 14th day after the meeting
mpc_framework.monetary_policy_report: Published by RBI once every six months, explaining sources of inflation and forecasts for 6-18 months ahead

inflation_targeting.review_period: Fixed every 5 years by Central Government in consultation with RBI (under Section 45ZA)
inflation_targeting.failure_definition: RBI fails to meet the inflation target if the average headline inflation is more than 6% or less than 2% for three consecutive quarters
inflation_targeting.consequence_of_failure: RBI must submit a report to the Central Government stating: (a) Reasons for failure, (b) Remedial actions proposed, (c) Estimated time period within which target will be achieved

policy_stances.name: Accommodative
policy_stances.meaning: RBI is ready to expand money supply and cut interest rates to boost economic growth. A rate hike is ruled out.
policy_stances.economic_context: Economic slowdown, recessionary pressures, or post-crisis recovery.

policy_stances.name: Neutral
policy_stances.meaning: RBI can move interest rates in either direction (increase or decrease) or keep them unchanged depending on incoming data.
policy_stances.economic_context: Balanced economic growth with inflation around target.

policy_stances.name: Calibrated Tightening / Hawkish
policy_stances.meaning: RBI signals that interest rates may be hiked or kept steady, but a rate cut is off the table.
policy_stances.economic_context: Rising inflationary pressures and overheating economy.

policy_stances.name: Withdrawal of Accommodation
policy_stances.meaning: Gradually reducing excess liquidity injected during crisis periods to bring policy back to neutral/non-inflationary conditions.

quantitative_tools.name: Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)
quantitative_tools.description: Specified minimum percentage of total Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) that scheduled banks must maintain as unencumbered cash balance with the RBI.
quantitative_tools.interest_earned: RBI pays NO interest to banks on CRR deposits (since 2007).
quantitative_tools.floor_ceiling: The RBI (Amendment) Act 2006 removed the statutory floor (3%) and ceiling (20%). RBI has full discretion.
quantitative_tools.impact_of_increase: Reduces bank lending capacity, contracts money supply, curbs inflation.
quantitative_tools.impact_of_decrease: Infuses liquidity into banking system, promotes credit growth.

quantitative_tools.name: Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)
quantitative_tools.description: Specified percentage of NDTL that banks must maintain in liquid assets with themselves in the form of: Cash, Gold, or Approved Central/State Government Securities (G-Secs/T-Bills).
quantitative_tools.interest_earned: Banks earn interest on SLR G-Secs and coupon yield.
quantitative_tools.ceiling: Maximum ceiling is 40% (floor of 25% was removed in 2007 amendment).
quantitative_tools.impact: Ensures bank solvency, compels banks to invest in government debt, regulates credit flow.

quantitative_tools.name: Repo Rate (Repurchase Option)
quantitative_tools.description: The fixed interest rate at which RBI injects overnight/short-term liquidity to commercial banks against the pledge of eligible government securities.
quantitative_tools.mechanism: Banks borrow from RBI by selling G-Secs with an agreement to repurchase them at an agreed price/rate.
quantitative_tools.tenor: Overnight Repo and Term Repos (7 days, 14 days, 28 days).

quantitative_tools.name: Standing Deposit Facility (SDF)
quantitative_tools.section: Section 17(1A) of RBI Act, 1934 (empowered in 2018, operationalised April 2022)
quantitative_tools.description: Collateral-free liquidity absorption mechanism where banks can park surplus funds with RBI without RBI having to provide collateral/G-Secs.
quantitative_tools.significance: Replaced the Fixed Reverse Repo as the lower bound (floor) of the LAF corridor. Rate is pegged 25 bps below Repo.

quantitative_tools.name: Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)
quantitative_tools.introduced: May 2011 on recommendations of Working Group on Operating Procedure of Monetary Policy (Deepak Mohanty)
quantitative_tools.description: Penal liquidity window for scheduled commercial banks to borrow overnight funds from RBI above their normal LAF quota by dipping into their SLR portfolio up to a prescribed limit (usually 2% of NDTL).
quantitative_tools.rate: Pegged 25 bps above the Repo rate. Acts as ceiling of LAF corridor.

quantitative_tools.name: Bank Rate
quantitative_tools.description: Standard rate at which RBI is prepared to buy or rediscount bills of exchange or other commercial papers. Currently used as penal rate on shortfall in CRR/SLR.

quantitative_tools.name: Open Market Operations (OMO)
quantitative_tools.description: Outright purchase and sale of Government Securities in the open market to absorb or inject durable liquidity on a long-term basis.
quantitative_tools.variants: Operation Twist (simultaneous buying of long-term G-Secs and selling of short-term G-Secs to flatten the yield curve without altering aggregate money supply).

qualitative_tools.name: Margin Requirements / LTV (Loan to Value Ratio)
qualitative_tools.description: Difference between market value of security offered and loan sanctioned. E.g. If margin is 20%, maximum loan is 80% of asset value. Raising margin discourages speculative borrowing.

qualitative_tools.name: Moral Suasion
qualitative_tools.description: Informal advice, periodic meetings, exhortations, and persuasive appeals by RBI to banks to follow monetary objectives without formal statutory orders.

qualitative_tools.name: Credit Rationing
qualitative_tools.description: Fixing maximum ceilings or quotas of credit for specific sectors or purposes to curb over-lending in speculative areas.

qualitative_tools.name: Direct Action
qualitative_tools.description: Statutory penal action, fines, refusal of rediscounting, or supervisory restrictions imposed on non-compliant banks under Section 47A of BR Act.

steps: Cost of funds for commercial banks rises
Banks hike Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate (MCLR) & External Benchmark Linked Rate (EBLR)
Home loan, car loan & commercial loan EMIs increase
Borrowing slows down; consumer spending and corporate capital expenditure moderate
Aggregate demand decreases, controlling price levels and headline inflation
Cost of funds for commercial banks drops
Banks reduce lending rates for retail and corporate borrowers
Cheaper loans stimulate investment and consumption expenditure
Economic output and GDP growth receive positive momentum

exam_traps.trap: Believing RBI pays 4% interest to banks on their CRR balances.
exam_traps.fact: RBI pays ZERO interest on CRR balances maintained by banks (RBI Act Section 42 was amended in 2007).
Reverse Repo requires RBI to transfer G-Secs as collateral to banks. SDF is uncollateralised (RBI does NOT pledge any securities to absorb liquidity).

exam_traps.trap: Believing the MPC target is based on WPI (Wholesale Price Index).
exam_traps.fact: Monetary Policy target is strictly based on CPI-Combined (Consumer Price Index), as recommended by the Urjit Patel Committee (2014).

exam_traps.trap: Assuming the Government of India has 4 members and RBI has 2 members in the MPC.
exam_traps.fact: MPC has exactly 6 members: 3 from RBI and 3 appointed by Government of India.
